correctness.rationale: The binary scattered-subsequence counts reduce bijectively to (one-count t, weighted zero-based one-index sum J). Every even-length factor is exactly an even-start E(u) or odd-start O(u) image of an occurring half-length factor, with no missing boundary positions; both maps have \(t_{\mathrm{new}}=m-t\), \(J(E)=m^2-2J-t\) and \(J(O)=m(m-1)-2J\). At old outer weights, \(t_{\mathrm{new}}\) is odd, so E/O J parities differ and the two injective profile images are disjoint. At central weight \(t=2^k\), images are arithmetic progressions of common spacing \(2^{k+1}\) displaced by one spacing, giving \(k+4\) terms and the displayed minimum recurrence. The length-three base exhausts five factors. Therefore all k follow inductively. The packaged program independently and exhaustively checks all factor profiles for \(0\le k\le13\) using the three valid adjacent-letter pairs; a separate valuation-generated prefix agrees through \(k=10\). No finite test is treated as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The most direct prior comparison is Lejeune 2021 §4.5, pp115–117, which inspects this exact word and its 2-binomial complexity, shows a finite plot through length 70 and a qualitative power-of-two/non-power comparison, and states that precise values were not obtained. The theorem here determines an infinite non-dyadic family and each exact Hamming-weight layer, which cannot be deduced from those qualitative comparisons alone. Rigo–Salimov 2013 develops the invariant on other word families, and Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland 2022 §7.1 does not supply this formula. Searches of relevant indexed and published sources uncovered no matching earlier word-specific theorem, although an unindexed prior proof could exist.

value.rationale: The previous direct period-doubling analysis had qualitative dyadic versus non-dyadic information and a bounded plot but no exact infinite non-dyadic spectrum. The proved tripled-dyadic family determines infinitely many values with a nontrivial additive logarithmic term: \(b(3\cdot2^k)=2^{k+1}+k+3\), a distinct exact profile for all three Hamming weights, and a closed central arithmetic progression. These are natural 2-binomial invariants, not arbitrary parameters; the result supplies structural data about how the substitution refines scattering statistics. It neither claims an all-length formula nor needs a separate application theorem to be meaningful.
